blocks.prompt: 1. Find the \(8^{\text{th}}\) term of the arithmetico-geometric sequence, where the arithmetic part is \(1, 4, 7, \ldots\) and the geometric part is \(5, 10, 20, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
Arithmetico-geometric sequence (A.G.P.) ka har term do numbers ka product hota hai: ek A.P. se aur ek usi jagah wala G.P. se.
Is liye 8th term nikalne ke liye humein A.P. \(1, 4, 7, \ldots\) ka 8th term aur G.P. \(5, 10, 20, \ldots\) ka 8th term chahiye.
Plan: dono 8th terms apne apne formula se nikalo, phir multiply kar do. Saare terms likh kar ginne ki zaroorat nahi.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: A.P. part \(1, 4, 7, \ldots\) (\(a = 1, d = 3\)); G.P. part \(5, 10, 20, \ldots\) (\(b = 5, r = 2\))
Humein find karna hai: 8th term \(T_8\).
Tareeqa: A.G.P. ka \(n\)th term = (A.P. part ka \(n\)th term) \(\times\) (G.P. part ka \(n\)th term), yani \(T_n = [a + (n - 1)d]\,br^{n-1}\). A.P. ka term \(a + (n - 1)d\) aur G.P. ka term \(br^{n-1}\) alag alag nikalte hain, phir dono ko multiply kar dete hain.

A.P. part ka 8th term
\[a_8 = a + 7d\]
\[= 1 + 7(3) = 22\]
Kyun: A.P. mein \(d = 4 - 1 = 3\) hai. Pehle term se 8th term tak pohanchne ke liye \(d\) saat (7) dafa jama hota hai, aath dafa nahi, is liye \(n - 1 = 7\).

G.P. part ka 8th term
\[b_8 = br^{7}\]
\[= 5 \cdot 2^{7}\]
\[= 5 \times 128 = 640\]
Kyun: G.P. mein ratio \(r = 10 \div 5 = 2\) hai, aur \(n\)th term \(br^{n-1}\) hota hai, is liye power \(8 - 1 = 7\) hai. \(2^7 = 128\), aur \(5 \times 128 = 640\).
Dhyan dein: power 8 lagana aam ghalti hai; pehle term par power 0 hoti hai.

Dono 8th terms multiply karein
\[T_8 = a_8 \times b_8\]
\[= 22 \times 640\]
\[= 14080\]
Kyun: A.G.P. ka 8th term = A.P. ka 8th term \(\times\) G.P. ka 8th term. Hisaab aasaan karne ke liye \(22 = 20 + 2\) socho: \(20 \times 640 = 12800\) aur \(2 \times 640 = 1280\), jama \(14080\).

List bana kar tasdeeq
\[1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22\]
\[5, 10, 20, \ldots, 320, 640\]
Kyun: Dono parts ke pehle aath terms likh kar dekhein: A.P. ka aathwan 22 aur G.P. ka aathwan 640 hai. Formula wala jawab bilkul sahi hai.
